entries.84580de2783fe615: This region sells drugs in North America and is the largest of the five regions in both revenue and segment profit. Eisai Corporation of North America, the Americas holding company, Eisai Inc. (US), which conducts R&D, manufacturing and sales of pharmaceuticals, and Eisai Ltd. (Canada), which sells, are responsible for this region. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥300,440 million (¥300.4 billion, up 8.0% year on year), and segment profit was ¥174,375 million (¥174.4 billion, up 10.2%). By product, Lenvima accounted for the bulk at ¥237.2 billion (up 2.1%), Leqembi ¥44.6 billion (up 70.7%) and Dayvigo ¥10.5 billion (up 53.5%). In October 2025, the subcutaneous autoinjector formulation of Leqembi, LEQEMBI IQLIK, was launched in the US, and in December 2025 Leqembi was launched in Canada. Of the three companies that the annual securities report lists as principal customers of the company's total revenue, two, McKesson Corporation (¥86,034 million) and Cencora,Inc. (¥75,379 million), are customers in this region. Note that this region covers North America only; Central and South America fall under East Asia & Global South.
entries.85ed6de01a5a83c3: This region sells drugs in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Russia and Oceania. The region is run under Eisai Europe Ltd. (UK), the European holding company, by Eisai Ltd. and Eisai Manufacturing Ltd. (UK), which conduct R&D and manufacturing, and by sales companies in Germany, France, Spain, Italy and others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥81,532 million (¥81.5 billion, up 2.7%), fourth among the five regions. Segment profit was ¥30,412 million (¥30.4 billion), and the company explains that it fell 15.4% year on year due to the impact of structural reforms. By product, Lenvima/Kisplyx was ¥49.2 billion (up 17.4%), Fycompa ¥17.3 billion (up 10.6%) and Leqembi ¥1.6 billion. Leqembi's launch began in this fiscal year, starting with Austria in August 2025, followed by Germany, Saudi Arabia, Finland and Portugal.

entries.9b48cdddc1093b01: This business does not sell pharmaceuticals themselves; the annual securities report describes it as a business related to license income from the parent company and pharmaceutical raw materials. The business description table lists licenses, pharmaceutical raw materials and business services as main products, and shows the company and Sunplanet Co., Ltd., which provides business services and others, as the responsible companies. In the status of affiliated companies, Arteryex Co., Ltd. (software planning and development), Theoria Technologies Co., Ltd. (healthcare-related services) and Ekonavista Co., Ltd. also belong to this business. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥14,599 million, segment profit was ¥4,508 million, and the number of employees was 711. This is a significant decline from ¥40,369 million in the previous fiscal year. By breakdown, license revenue fell from ¥29,159 million in the previous year to ¥1,297 million, and the company cites, in its overall explanation, the recording in the previous year of a lump-sum payment related to the transfer of rights to some products.

entries.a394e399ec420668: This business researches, develops, manufactures and sells prescription drugs dispensed at hospitals and over-the-counter drugs sold at pharmacies, and most of Eisai Co., Ltd.'s revenue comes from it. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] divides the Pharmaceutical Business by region into five (Japan, Americas (North America), China, EMEA (Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Russia and Oceania), and East Asia & Global South (South Korea, Taiwan, India, ASEAN, Central and South America, South Africa, etc.)) and designates these five as [[term:segment|reportable segments]]. Total revenue of the five regions for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥810,779 million, accounting for most of the company's total revenue of ¥825,378 million. The company is focusing its efforts on neurology (centered on dementia) and oncology (centered on refractory cancers). Company-wide revenue by product was ¥362,668 million for oncology products, ¥260,568 million for neurology products and ¥202,142 million for other products. There are three key drugs. The anticancer drug Lenvima (revenue ¥342.5 billion) is a co-developed and co-promoted drug with US Merck, with which the company signed an agreement on March 7, 2018; the Alzheimer's disease treatment Leqembi (¥88.0 billion, up 98.7% year on year) is a co-developed and co-promoted drug with Biogen Inc. (US), with which it signed an agreement on March 4, 2014. The third is the insomnia treatment Dayvigo (¥64.3 billion, up 19.6% year on year). In addition, the segment profit of the five regions combined (¥367,323 million) does not include research and development expenses of ¥138,353 million that are not allocated to each region, or head office management costs and other items of the parent company totaling ¥189,340 million. The latter includes ¥158,204 million of profit sharing for Lenvima payable to US Merck; after deducting these items, the company's total operating profit was ¥44,138 million. The number of employees was 9,832 as of March 31, 2026.
entries.af748cd533545f40: This region manufactures and sells drugs in China. The region is run by Eisai (China) Investment Co., Ltd., the holding company that oversees China; Eisai (China) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and Eisai (Liaoning) Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., which manufacture and sell; Eisai (Suzhou) Trading Co., Ltd., which sells; and others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥130,745 million (¥130.7 billion, up 13.2%), and segment profit was ¥59,312 million (¥59.3 billion, up 3.7%), both third among the five regions. By product, Lenvima was ¥25.0 billion, Methycobal ¥12.6 billion, Merislon ¥12.5 billion (down 11.6%) and Leqembi ¥12.4 billion. Leqembi grew significantly, up 163.1% year on year, due to expanding demand. In July 2025, the gout treatment URECE was newly launched in China, and in August 2025, the insomnia treatment Dayvigo was launched in China.

entries.f91ccce758372238: This region sells drugs in Japan. This region is run by the company and EA Pharma Co., Ltd., which was formed in 2016 through integration with Ajinomoto Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. and is a [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiary]] with 60.00% voting rights. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥229,238 million (¥229.2 billion, up 6.0%), second among the five regions after Americas, and segment profit was ¥72,979 million (¥73.0 billion, up 1.8%), also second. The breakdown is prescription pharmaceuticals ¥206.7 billion and over-the-counter pharmaceuticals and others ¥22.5 billion. By product, Dayvigo was ¥46.5 billion, Leqembi ¥24.4 billion (up 91.3%), Jyseleca ¥18.4 billion, Lenvima ¥14.1 billion, Gūfisu ¥8.8 billion, Mobikōru ¥8.7 billion and Fycompa ¥8.2 billion. In over-the-counter pharmaceuticals and others, the Chocola BB Group was ¥15.9 billion, and in June 2025 the company newly launched the OTC proton pump inhibitor Pariet S. Among the principal customers of the company's total revenue, Medipal Holdings Corporation (¥59,202 million) is listed as a customer in this region.
entries.fc4c9edc8ebdfe4b: This region sells drugs in South Korea, Taiwan, India, ASEAN, Central and South America, South Africa and others. The region is run by Eisai Asia Regional Services Pte. Ltd. in Singapore, Weicai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. in Taiwan, and sales companies in Thailand, South Korea and India, among others. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥68,823 million (¥68.8 billion, up 15.6%), and segment profit was ¥30,245 million (¥30.2 billion, up 10.5%). Both are the smallest of the five regions, while the revenue growth rate is the highest of the five regions. By product, Lenvima was ¥17.1 billion, Aricept ¥14.6 billion and Leqembi ¥5.0 billion (¥0.4 billion in the previous year). Leqembi was launched in Taiwan and Singapore in June 2025, in Mexico in September and in Thailand in November.
